text:
**About 300–400 W of panels recharges a 1,000 Wh station from empty in one sunny day. About 200 W does it in roughly 1.5 days.**

## The math

Panels rarely deliver their rated watts. Heat, sun angle and charging losses mean you should plan on about 70–75% of the label rating ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge), [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).

**Panel watts ≈ 1,000 Wh ÷ (peak sun hours × 0.75)**

| Sun conditions | Peak sun hours | Panel watts for a 1-day refill |
|---|---|---|
| Northern winter | 2 | ~700 W+ |
| Average US day | 4 | ~340 W |
| Good summer day | 5 | ~270–300 W |
| Southwest or strong summer | 6 | ~230 W |

Figures are from [power-runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/) and [Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/).

If you don't need a one-day refill, divide the station's watt-hours by 5. That gives about **200 W**, which puts back roughly 630 Wh a day and refills the station in about 1.5 days ([Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station)).

## Check your station's specs first

1. **Maximum solar input (watts).** Panels beyond this limit won't charge faster on a sunny day, though a little extra helps in clouds and in morning or evening light.
2. **Input voltage range.** The panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay inside the station's range. Panels wired in series add their voltages together, and going over the limit can damage the station.
3. **Connector.** Most panels use MC4 connectors. Make sure you have the adapter for your station's port, such as XT60 or a DC barrel plug.

## Example panel

The **ALLPOWERS SP037 400 W foldable panel** would refill a 1,000 Wh station in one average day. It's $299, or $269.10 with code ALLPOWERS26 (the listing says the code was tested on Oct 21 and expires Dec 30, 2026). **[Buy at ALLPOWERS](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel)**. This is an affiliate link ([source](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel)).
- Voc is 45.3 V, so it suits stations that accept 12–60 V. It's too high for stations limited to 24–28 V.
- It weighs 18.5 kg (about 41 lb), which is heavy for a folding panel.
